title: The Hospital
dek: A hospital cut open from the helipad to A&E: the people, the rooms and what happens in them.
frames: The … is on the ground / first / second floor.
You go to the … when you …

truefalse.s: The ambulance is outside the hospital.
The doctor has got a stethoscope.
There are two beds in the ward.
The pharmacy is on the ground floor.
There is a computer at reception.
The patient in the waiting room has got his arm in a sling.
The nurse is holding a clipboard.
The wheelchair is in the ward.
There are some flowers next to a bed.
The lift is between the first and second floors.
The surgeon is wearing a mask.
The patient on the drip is next to the window.
The operating theatre is above A&E.
The paramedic is pushing a wheelchair.
The helipad is on the roof.
The prescription is on the doctor's desk.
The first aid kit is in the pharmacy.

A1: Who works in a hospital? What do they do?
Look at the ward. Write five sentences: There is… There are…
When did you last see a doctor? Why?
A2: You are at reception. Write a dialogue: say who you are and what's wrong.
Describe what is happening on each floor of the hospital. Use the present continuous.
Your friend has broken a leg. Write a get-well-soon message.
B1: Would you like to work in a hospital? Which job, and why?
Explain what happens when someone arrives in A&E, step by step.
Should hospital car parks be free for patients and visitors? Give your reasons.

rooms.ex: My grandad is in hospital with a broken leg.
rooms.def: A building where sick or hurt people are looked after by doctors and nurses.

rooms.ex: Please go to reception and give your name.
rooms.def: The place near the entrance where you say who you are and why you have come.

rooms.ex: We sat in the waiting room for an hour.
rooms.def: A room where you sit until it is your turn.

rooms.ex: He cut his hand and went to A&E.
rooms.def: Accident and Emergency: the part of a hospital for people who are badly hurt or suddenly very ill.
A big room in a hospital with beds for patients.

rooms.ex: The patient is in the operating theatre now.
rooms.def: The room where doctors do operations.

rooms.ex: Take this form to the X-ray department on the second floor.
rooms.def: The part of a hospital where they take X-rays.

rooms.ex: The doctor will see you in the consulting room.
rooms.def: The room where a doctor talks to you and examines you.

rooms.ex: You can collect your medicine from the pharmacy.
rooms.def: The place where you get medicine.

parts.ex: Call an ambulance - quickly!
parts.def: A vehicle that takes ill or hurt people to hospital.

parts.ex: We heard the siren and moved to the side of the road.
parts.def: The loud sound and flashing lights on an ambulance or police car.

parts.ex: Meet me at the main entrance.
parts.def: The door or way into a building.

parts.ex: The air ambulance landed on the helipad on the roof.
parts.def: A flat place where a helicopter can land.

parts.ex: Take the lift to the second floor.
parts.def: A small room that carries people up and down in a building.

parts.ex: The receptionist asked for my name and date of birth.
parts.def: The person at reception who welcomes visitors and answers questions.

parts.ex: Your details are on the computer.
parts.def: An electronic machine for storing information and working with it.

parts.ex: There are no free chairs in the waiting room.
parts.def: Seats for one person, with a back.

parts.ex: The patient is waiting to see the doctor.
parts.def: A person who is ill or hurt and is being looked after by a doctor.

parts.ex: She had her arm in a sling for three weeks.
parts.def: A piece of cloth around your neck that holds a hurt arm.

parts.ex: The visiting times are on the noticeboard.
parts.def: A board on a wall where people put up information.

parts.ex: They carried him out on a stretcher.
parts.def: A bed on wheels for moving people who cannot walk.

parts.ex: The paramedics arrived in five minutes.
parts.def: A person who works on an ambulance and helps people in an emergency.

parts.ex: The nurse brought a wheelchair to the door.
parts.def: A chair with wheels for people who cannot walk.

parts.ex: He'll need crutches for a month.
parts.def: Two sticks that help you walk when you have hurt your leg.

parts.ex: There's a first aid kit in every classroom.
parts.def: A box with bandages, plasters and things to help someone who is hurt.

parts.ex: The patient has to stay in bed today.
parts.def: A piece of furniture that you sleep on.

parts.ex: The nurse put a clean bandage on his head.
parts.def: A long piece of cloth that you put around a hurt part of the body.

parts.ex: We brought Mum some flowers.
parts.def: The coloured part of a plant; people bring them to someone in hospital.

parts.ex: The nurse closed the curtain around the bed.
parts.def: A piece of cloth you pull around a bed so the patient is not seen.

parts.ex: She was on a drip for two days.
parts.def: A bag of liquid that goes slowly into a patient's arm through a tube.

parts.ex: The nurse checks on the patients every hour.
parts.def: A person who looks after people in hospital.

parts.ex: The nurse wrote the temperature on her clipboard.
parts.def: A board that holds papers, so you can write while you stand.

parts.ex: The surgeon has done hundreds of operations like this.
parts.def: A doctor who does operations.

parts.ex: Everyone in the theatre wears a mask.
parts.def: A thing you wear over your mouth and nose to stop germs.

parts.ex: The patient was lifted onto the operating table.
parts.def: The table a patient lies on during an operation.

parts.ex: The surgeon moved the lamp closer.
parts.def: A light. In an operating theatre it is very bright.

parts.ex: The heart monitor started beeping.
parts.def: A screen that shows how a patient's heart is beating.

parts.ex: The X-ray shows that her finger is broken.
parts.def: A photo of the inside of your body, showing the bones.

parts.ex: Lie still on the table under the X-ray machine.
parts.def: The machine that takes X-rays.

parts.ex: You should see a doctor about that cough.
parts.def: A person whose job is to help ill people get better.

parts.ex: The doctor listened to my chest with a stethoscope.
parts.def: The thing a doctor uses to listen to your heart and breathing.

parts.ex: Read the fourth line of the eye chart, please.
parts.def: A board with letters that get smaller, for testing your eyes.

parts.ex: The doctor sat down at her desk.
parts.def: A table you work at.

parts.ex: Take this prescription to the pharmacy.
parts.def: A paper from a doctor that says what medicine you need.

parts.ex: Stand on the scales, please.
parts.def: A machine that shows how heavy you are.

parts.ex: Ask the pharmacist how often to take it.
parts.def: A person whose job is to prepare and sell medicine.

parts.ex: Take this medicine three times a day.
parts.def: Something you take to get better when you are ill.

parts.ex: Take two pills after breakfast.
parts.def: Small round pieces of medicine that you swallow.

parts.ex: Have you got a plaster? I've cut my finger.
parts.def: Small sticky pieces of cloth for covering a small cut.
